full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 27-11-2007 (decree signed on 6-1-2008) passed by the learned Special Joint District Judge and Paribesh Adalat, Dhaka in Civil Appeal No.36 of 2007 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 28- 1-2007 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.39 of 2003 dismissing the suit should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 6. The learned Assistant Judge, Dhaka after hearing by his judgment and decree dated 28-1- 2007 dismissed the suit on contest. 

 7. The unsuccessful plaintiff, thereafter, preferred Other Appeal No.36 of 2007 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka which was subsequently transferred to the Court of learned Special Joint District Judge and Paribesh Adalat, Dhaka, who by the impugned judgment and decreed dated 27-11-2007 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court on the finding that the plaintiff is a defaulter in payment of rent and the plaintiff brought the suit with unclean hands and the instant revision application is directed against that judgment. 

 23. Taking into consideration of all these aspects of the case, I find there is a good deal of substance in the contention raised by the learned Advocate for the defendant-opposite party that the suit itself was incompetent and not maintainable and accept the same. By now I have covered all the points raised by the learned Advocates for both the sides. The learned Judge of the appellate court appears to have considered all the material aspects of the case and justly upheld the judgment and decree of the trial Court. I find no reason to interfere therewith.
